text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> 🔔 SEV-2: Elevated tail latency observed for tenant Cerulean Health (dedicated-pool-7, VPC). p99 token latency > 2.5s, tenant_queue_wait_ms spike started 2026-03-15T02:09:03Z. Paging oncall.

mira: oncall here. grabbing context — is this isolated to one shard or across the pool?

sam: looks concentrated on shard-3 and shard-4 of pool-7, but the routing facade still sends to all. metric `tenant_queue_wait_ms` for cerulean jumped 20ms -> 1200ms. batch formation time increased. GPU and CPU are within normal util.

devin: I pulled the request histogram. Cerulean traffic changed ~01:50Z — many tiny requests (1-4 tokens). Downstream batch sizes collapsed, scheduler doing too many small batches; overheads dominate. Also a cron job from their side started spiking qps.

jules-se: customer reporting chat app feels laggy. They confirmed they pushed a client-side telemetry job around 01:47Z. Only Cerulean impacted, others on same pool steady.

mira: ok want to avoid pool-wide knobs. We'll do tenant-level overrides: reduce max_batch_tokens to bound formation time, and lower max_batch_latency_ms so we don't wait long for small requests. Proposal: max_batch_tokens=1024, max_batch_latency_ms=30. Also enable small-batch coalescing for that tenant to allow the scheduler to group tiny requests onto existing in-flight batches.

sam: +1. Also suggest bumping `instant_merge_window_ms` from 5 -> 15 for cerulean so tiny arrivals can merge with a warm batch.

devin: crafting config change. tenant override YAML ready: 
```
tenant_overrides:
  cerulean-health:
    scheduler:
      max_batch_tokens: 1024
      max_batch_latency_ms: 30
      instant_merge_window_ms: 15
      adaptive_small_batch_threshold: 0.5
```
Applying to pool-7 sharded rollout (shard-3 first).

incident-bot: Config rollout started by devin at 2026-03-15T02:18:42Z. Change ID cfg-38922. Rolling to pool-shard-3 -> shard-4 -> remainder.

alex-sre: watch: within 25s of shard-3 rollout, queue_wait_ms dropped ~1200ms -> 140ms. p99 token latency fell 2.6s -> ~0.85s. No new 5xx from that shard.

mira: great. sam, run a small canary replay and diff generation to ensure output sanity. we need to check model behaviour not affected.

sam: kicked off tools/replay/canary_replay.sh --tenant cerulean-health --qps 25 --duration 90. First run: error rate stable, token-level diffs tiny (mostly punctuation). latency improves across all quantiles.

jules-se: customer on the thread says interactive latency better but they see occasional 500s for long-running completions (>2048 tokens). Looks like our smaller max_batch_tokens is truncating planned batching margin for large requests.

mira: good point. plan: implement tiered routing. Short requests (<2048 est tokens) use the new low-latency scheduler overrides. Long requests (>2048) route to a large-batch path: increase max_batch_tokens=8192 and max_batch_latency_ms=200 for those requests. That keeps interactive fast but preserves throughput for long jobs.

devin: we can add a request_estimated_tokens routing rule. Draft override: 
```
tenant_overrides:
  cerulean-health:
    scheduler:
      default:
        max_batch_tokens: 1024
        max_batch_latency_ms: 30
      large_request:
        selector: request_estimated_tokens > 2048
        max_batch_tokens: 8192
        max_batch_latency_ms: 200
```
Applying as staged rollout.

incident-bot: Change cfg-38923 started by devin at 2026-03-15T02:34:10Z. Canary applied to shard-4 for large_request rule.

alex-sre: observing shard-4 — long-job queue for cerulean still sees occasional 500s but those appear tied to a single worker hitting mem spike and OOM-kill from a legacy debug container. Not directly due to scheduler. I've started remediation: draining that worker.

sam: replay indicates large_request path returns correct outputs and latencies as expected. No regression.

jules-se: I updated Cerulean support lead: we pushed low-latency mode for interactive and a separate path for long jobs; they report interactive flows look normal. They've paused their midnight telemetry to monitor.

mira: stabilization window: keep these overrides for 1 hour, monitor p99 and errors. If stable, we'll codify as permanent tenant profile and schedule a follow-up with Cerulean to discuss client-side batching/backoff. Assign follow-ups:
- ops-lead: coordinate postmortem and customer readout
- devin: add automated tenant-level canary for future big config changes
- sam: run 1-hour tracer to validate no tail regressions
- alex-sre: verify drained worker is recovered and no residual 500s

ops-lead: taking postmortem lead. We'll capture timeline, config deltas, and recommend client-side rate shaping. Also want to add a dashboard for per-tenant small-batch fraction to detect regressions early.

mira: handoff time ~2026-03-15T03:02Z — I'm logging out, ops-lead you've got the incident. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: SEV-2 acknowledged by ops-lead at 2026-03-15T03:02:45Z. Next steps: monitor for 60m and close if stable.
